response.overview: In [paˈlʲit͡sʲ], the Białowieża Forest—a landscape divided between Poland and Belarus by a 170-kilometre steel and barbed-wire border wall—becomes both protagonist and storyteller, tracing the wounds of humanitarian and ecological crisis. Older than the border that cuts through it, the forest undermines dominant narratives of territory and reminds us that “every living thing is both indigenous and a migrant.”
response.title: [paˈlʲit͡sʲ]
